title: Building an Award Winning Service Culture
overview: Outstanding customer service is not created by isolated acts of courtesy or by frontline employees alone. It is the result of an organizational culture in which customer value, service standards, employee behavior, leadership practices, processes, communication, measurement, and continuous improvement consistently support the desired customer experience.

This course provides a practical framework for building and sustaining a high-performance service culture. Participants will examine what distinguishes service excellence from basic service delivery, define customer expectations and moments that matter, translate service values into observable behaviors and standards, align employees and processes around the customer journey, strengthen service recovery, and use feedback and performance measures to drive improvement.

The program emphasizes both leadership responsibility and everyday employee behavior. Through practical exercises, service scenarios, customer-journey analysis, standards development, and improvement planning, participants will develop an actionable approach for creating a service culture that is consistent, distinctive, measurable, and sustainable.
audience: Managers, supervisors, team leaders, customer-service managers, contact-center leaders, service-quality personnel, customer-experience professionals, operations managers, branch managers, front-office personnel, HR and learning professionals, and employees responsible for improving customer satisfaction, service standards, employee service behavior, or the overall customer experience.
methodology: The course uses an interactive methodology combining short presentations, service-culture diagnostics, customer-experience case studies, customer-journey mapping, service-standard workshops, role plays, communication exercises, complaint and recovery scenarios, root-cause analysis, performance-measurement activities, group discussions, and action planning. Participants will apply the concepts to their own service environment and develop practical service-culture improvement initiatives.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Explain the characteristics of a strong service culture and how it differs from isolated customer-service initiatives.
Identify customer expectations, needs, pain points, and critical moments across the service journey.
Translate service values into clear, observable, and measurable service behaviors.
Develop practical service standards for different customer touchpoints.
Strengthen internal service relationships that influence the external customer experience.
Apply effective communication behaviors in face-to-face, telephone, and digital customer interactions.
Handle complaints and service failures using structured service-recovery practices.
Use customer feedback and service data to identify improvement priorities.
Define service-performance measures that support customer and organizational objectives.
Recognize the leadership practices required to reinforce and sustain service excellence.
Develop a practical action plan for strengthening the service culture within the organization.
